message.content:
The title “best jazz singer” is highly subjective and depends on what you value—vocal technique, emotional depth, influence, or innovation. However, a few names consistently appear at the top of most lists and are widely regarded as the pinnacle of jazz vocal artistry:

| Singer | Why they’re considered among the best |
|--------|---------------------------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable pitch, scat‑scoring mastery, and effortless phrasing set a standard for jazz vocalists. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her deeply emotive delivery, unique phrasing, and ability to convey complex feelings made her a pioneer in jazz interpretation. |
| **Louis Armstrong** (as a vocalist) | Though primarily a trumpeter, his gravelly voice and charismatic stage presence helped popularize jazz worldwide. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | A modern icon whose blend of jazz, pop, and soul showcases technical brilliance and contemporary relevance. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | A contemporary legend whose powerful voice and improvisational skill keep her at the forefront of modern jazz. |

If you’re looking for a single “best” singer, many would argue that **Ella Fitzgerald** stands out due to her unmatched vocal control, versatility across styles, and lasting influence on generations of musicians. Nonetheless, the beauty of jazz lies in its diversity, so exploring multiple voices will give you a richer appreciation of the genre.
